contexts.text: They had been zealous only for themselves and the world.
They take pains to put off (this sphere of commanding).
Their sphere took from me all power of application. SE 2502.
One who had been devoted to studies. AC 3474. SE 2053.
They who had been studious for the sake of the memory only...
This was their study of wisdom.
These (Knowledges) are learned... partly by the man's own study.
If he is zealous more for the neighbour and the Lord than for himself, he is in a state of regeneration... But if he is zealous more for himself... he is in no state of regeneration.
That there would then be a full state of study. Signified, Explained.
For the labour of the external man is study in the internal. Hence study is called the labour of the mind.
Holy study. Signified, Explained... That is called holy study by which internal truths are conjoined with good.
The truths of the external man... he acquired... at last by his own study.
To serve = labour and study.
Labour and study from His Own power. Signified, Explained.
They seek wealth with the most intense application.
Devotedness of life according to the precepts of faith, is to watch.
He then studies life more than doctrine.
For they who study the Word, know it.
From childhood to adolescence, communication is opened to the interior Natural by learning... both by instruction... and by their own studies.
Such Spirits... had not been devoted to any self-application (here), not even domestic. Described. (They induce diseases. DMin 4730.)
The light of truth (then) falls into such things as are of the body and the world, which they exclusively busy themselves with.
He dwelt near a well = studious application there in the Word. To dwell = life; here, the studious application of the life.
No work shall be done... = no labours and pursuits which have for their end the things of the world.
That they must devote themselves to these things only. Signified.
To sin is to do and think what is evil and false intentionally...
No imitation from the busying himself of man. Signified, Explained.
That which is done from man, and from his busying himself, is done from his proprium, and is not holy; because a busying from the proprium of man is nothing but what is false from what is evil...
The learned at this day are not delighted with such a study (of the Word).
(With the ancients) this was the study of their wisdom.
(Thus) by their own exertion they exclude their children from Heaven.
He who is delighted with studies, reads and writes (there) as before.
They who have studied sciences merely to be accounted learned...
They who have studied the Word from the affection of knowing truth...
Uses for perfecting the Rational, are all things which... are called knowledges and branches of study...
Thy labour and endurance = their study and patience. (Compare AE 98.)
Their study and exertion to procure... the things of religion and its doctrine. Signified, Explained.
Thy faith and endurance = the Truth and the study to procure and teach it... Endurance = the study and labour of procuring and teaching it.
They who study the doctrine of justification by faith alone, who are called the clergy. Signified, Explained.
The love of use, and the consequent busying of one's self in use, holds the mind together...
The study of our Age was the study of Truths... This study was the study of our souls and minds; but the representations of Truths in forms were the study of the senses of our bodies...
In the World of Spirits and in Heaven there are... studies of all branches of learning.
Everyone has conjugial love with its virtue... according to his application to the genuine use in which he is.
No determination to any study or business (a cause of cold). Explained.

By study and business is meant all application to uses. When a man is in any study and business, that is, in use, his mind is limited and circumscribed as in a circle, within which it is successively coordinated into a form truly human, from which as from a house he sees various concupiscences outside of himself, and from the soundness of reason within he banishes them...
It is granted to (evil Spirits) to apply their minds to some study or work, whereby they are kept in externals, and thus in a state of intelligence.
Even those who have been devoted to piety are perverted by them.
The Social Gatherings... were recreations of their souls from studies and labours.
Every artificer who is assiduous at his work performs it easily and willingly... In like manner everyone who is in any function, or in any study.
You say that... you have followed pursuits of piety...
Everyone can be regenerated according to his state... those in divers studies, and also in divers offices, in one way...
A Church which separates... the remission of sins from repentance and the pursuit of a new life.
Politics... sometimes withdraw the spirits (of the English) from studies of a more lofty judgment, by which a higher intelligence is acquired. They do indeed imbibe these things in their youth...
On the life after death of those who are continually intent on studies.
On those who (here) have been zealous solely for natural things.
From such a pursuit or labour they can expect no reward in Heaven, because it was for the sake of self...
(When a man is ruled by those who constitute the cuticle) he is withheld from all application...
On those who study solely the sense of the letter.
When one who inclines to uses... comes among such Spirits... all his application is torpified.
They hate those who are laborious and studious for truth and good.
Like beggars who... are thus kept back from all application to anything, so as to be members of civil society.
Such are those who are zealous for themselves only. Described. SE 2772, Explained.
The good Spirits... performed it with the greatest zeal.
Not from any endeavour on their part.
He had studied only such things as are instrumental causes for acquiring understanding; as mathematics, etc.
There was a vast number who studied books...
Those who study in the Heavens have communication with those in these public libraries, and are instructed thence in doubtful Things.
They receive the spiritual affection of truth when they study the good of life...
In one of the chambers, the delight is to study...
Those appear to themselves to grind (there) who study many things. They write and instruct themselves assiduously, without the end of use...
See Use.
Students of modern orthodoxy object that...
